newsitem.title: USA: U.S. deplores opposition arrests in Niger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. deplores opposition arrests in Niger.

text.p: The United States said on Thursday it was "deeply concerned" about the arrest of opposition leaders in Niger, a move it said showed the government's contempt for democracy and human rights.

Former president Mahamane Ousmane and two other opposition leaders were arrested following a turbulent weekend protest in the West African state. Witnesses said they had been transferred to unknown destinations.

"This latest repression of the peaceful political opposition clearly demonstrates the regime's continued determination to thwart democracy and basic human rights," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

"This is another deplorable step in the wake of the military's seizure of power a year ago and its conduct of fraudulent presidential elections in July. These actions inevitably undermine international confidence in Niger," Burns said in a statement.
The United States ended its aid programme to Niger following last year's coup.
Thursday's U.S. statement called on Niger to ensure the safety and well-being of those detained and to conduct any judicial procedures openly and fairly.
It also urged the government to bring about an early return to civilian, democratic rule.
